extracted.intended_audience: immigration stakeholders (applicants, sponsors), State governments, advocacy groups, immigration practitioners, and DHS/USCIS officers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules for applying the public charge ground of inadmissibility, including information-collection (Form I-485), public charge bonds, economic analysis methodology, and consideration of chilling effects and State impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-485 sufficiency / no supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS has determined that the Form I-485 sufficiently collects information regarding the factors that will be considered in a public charge inadmissibility determination and therefore will not create a supplement to Form I-485.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not creating a supplement reduces burden on noncitizens; most noncitizens not required to file an Affidavit of Support Under Section 213A will not need to provide information specifically related to this determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form question format and time burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-ended narrative-style questions proposed in the NPRM were changed to multiple-choice style questions to reduce applicant time burden; DHS reduced estimated Form I-485 completion time from 7.92 hours to 7.16 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time burden includes reviewing instructions, gathering required documentation and information, completing the application, preparing statements, attaching necessary documentation, and submitting the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum public charge bond amount
rubrics_metrics.description: When USCIS exercises discretion to offer a public charge bond in adjustment-of-status cases inadmissible only under section 212(a)(4) of the INA, USCIS will set the bond amount at no less than $1,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS declines proposals for a negligible $100 bond; $1,000 reflects the minimum amount to ensure Federal, State, local, tribal governments are held harmless against the noncitizen becoming a public charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of public charge bond and breach trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of a public charge bond is to hold the United States, States, territories, counties, towns, municipalities, and districts harmless against bonded immigrants becoming public charges; receiving public cash assistance for income maintenance or long-term institutionalization at government expense would result in a breach determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bond authority is exercised consistent with statutory purpose and prior practice; bonds are not designed to reimburse all government expenses but to ensure governments are held harmless.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS discretion in offering bonds (case-by-case)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will consider offering adjustment of status applicants a public charge bond in its discretion on a case-by-case, individualized basis and will not limit offering bonds to a specific number of cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will provide officers with guidance and training to ensure this discretionary authority is exercised fairly, efficiently, and consistently; decisions are individualized determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include provisions for bond cancellation and breach procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule includes provisions pertaining to USCIS' exercise of public charge bond authority in adjustment of status applications, as well as provisions pertaining to public charge bond cancellation and breach determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions aim to ensure public charge bonds remain operationally feasible in adjustment of status cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory baseline selection per OMB Circular A-4
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2019 Final Rule is not the appropriate baseline for the rule's economic analysis; the baseline should be 'the way the world would look absent the proposed action' per OMB Circular A-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory effects and alternatives should be compared against the legally appropriate baseline; previously finalized but no-longer-effective rules are not automatically the baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer payments treatment in economic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Reductions in transfer payments (e.g., reduced State public benefit expenditures due to disenrollment) are reallocations of money between groups and are treated as transfer payments rather than costs or benefits under OMB Circular A-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer payments do not affect total resources available to society and should be accounted for separately from costs and benefits in the Regulatory Impact Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and analysis of chilling effects
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS must consider chilling effects (disenrollment or forgone enrollment in public benefits due to fear or confusion) and their downstream consequences, including worsening health outcomes, increased ER use, communicable disease prevalence, uncompensated care, poverty, housing instability, and reduced productivity and educational attainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule’s analysis should include qualitative discussion of chilling effects where quantitative estimation is not possible and incorporate evidence (studies, surveys, enrollment data) on such effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between cash assistance and non-cash benefits for public charge probative value
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS draws a reasonable line between cash assistance for income maintenance (more probative of primary dependence) and supplemental or special-purpose non-cash benefits (less probative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction aligns with prior statutory and agency practice (e.g., IRCA, 1999 Interim Field Guidance) and justifies excluding many non-cash benefits from being dispositive of public-charge determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of regulatory alternatives (e.g., 2019-like Alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where DHS considers an Alternative similar to the 2019 Final Rule, it must analyze additional direct costs (e.g., forms required such as Form I-944), increased time burdens (estimates included), administrative costs, and transfer payment effects; DHS estimated the Alternative’s annual direct costs at ~ $62 million vs $6 million for the Final Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also estimate the Alternative’s effects on transfer payments (DHS estimates ~$3.79 billion lower transfer payments under the Alternative) and qualitatively assess indirect harms to populations not subject to public charge determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation methodology for unpaid time in cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS uses the effective minimum wage to value non-paid time and applies a benefits-to-wage multiplier; DHS declines to use rates consistent with those paid for similar work in the relevant labor market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective minimum wage provides a single objective measure across a wide variety of unpaid activities; benefits-to-wage multiplier incorporates paid leave, supplemental pay, insurance, retirement, and savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of State administrative burdens and data limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments alleging State administrative costs must be considered, but DHS may be unable to fully quantify State-level administrative costs due to lack of data; such costs are included qualitatively and incorporated where provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS incorporated commenter-provided detailed information on State administrative costs into Section IV.A.5.d and describes qualitative effects when quantitative data are unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule does not determine public benefit eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the statutory public charge ground nor this final rule governs eligibility for public benefits; the rule addresses only how public charge inadmissibility is assessed and who is subject to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS commits to clear communication and implementing guidance to minimize confusion about who is and is not subject to public charge inadmissibility; minimizing chilling effects is an implementation goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of applicant time burden to be estimated
rubrics_metrics.description: Time burden estimates for completing forms should include time for reviewing instructions, gathering required documentation and information, completing the application, preparing statements, attaching necessary documentation, and submitting the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-burden calculations should reflect the full sequence of tasks necessary to complete and submit the relevant immigration form(s).
